chunk_findings.detail: The filter `not GI.always(r) or GI.pinned(r)` keeps a rule that is both always-scope and pinned. The function’s own docstring says that when the charter is present, “a rule that applies to all work is left to it,” so that rule is already emitted by `CH.block`. For a rule record with `GI.always(r) == True` and `GI.pinned(r) == True`, the brief therefore contains the same rule line twice: once in the charter and once in the item-specific rules block. That duplication consumes an extra line of the `session.brief_max_tokens` budget for one record even though the code claims to leave always-scope rules to the charter. The filter should drop all `GI.always` records when the charter carries them, or use the exact set of rule ids `CH.block` actually emitted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py:_rules_block

chunk_findings.detail: The `charter` text is appended before the existing backstop truncation, but the backstop is explicitly designed for the case where `_fit_sections` returns a body over its `room` because a single heading alone exceeded its share. In that case `charter` is the trailing part of `text`, and `text = text[: max(0, budget * 4 - len(note))].rsplit("\n", 1)[0]` truncates from the right, discarding the charter before the truncation note is appended. This means the `set_aside` reservation does not actually protect the pinned always-scope rules when the budget is tight enough to hit the existing backstop; the brief returns without the required rule titles, contrary to the intent that pinned always-scope rules never be trimmed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/markdown.py:1127

chunk_findings.detail: `pinned = GuidanceRecord(..., title="Pinned law", ...)` uses a capital **P**, but the assertion checks for the lowercase substring `"pinned"`. A charter line rendered as `[r-pin] Pinned law` does not contain `"pinned"`, so this test fails on the fixed formatter even though the pinned rule is actually present. The check should be `"Pinned"` (or only `"r-pin" in got[0]`).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_guidance_budget.py:56

chunk_findings.detail: The change does not touch the path that B91e1d67c87 is about: `ddflow brief --for-agent` still goes through `ddflow/api/briefing.py` and its `decision_order` filtering, which the bug report says drops all 7 `kind=rule` records to 0. The newly added regression test only calls `lifecycle.brief` and checks that `r-charter{i}` appears in `data["text"]`; it never exercises the subagent-brief or claim-block paths on the reproduction input (7 advisory rules and 260+ decisions), so the bug can remain while this test passes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_guidance_budget.py:82

chunk_findings.detail: The first rule is appended before any capacity check, because `if out and ...` is false on the first iteration. When `session.rules_charter_tokens` is positive but too small for the lead plus the first rule line, the function still returns a non-empty body; with two or more rules it returns the first rule plus `- _1 more rules...`, and `block()` renders LEAD plus those body lines despite exceeding the configured token budget. Concrete input: two live rules and `tokens=1` yields two body lines from `lines()` (or one non-empty line for one rule), far over 1 token. This contradicts the module’s own “Bounded by `[session].rules_charter_tokens`” contract and can blow the session brief budget. The first line needs the same `used + approx_tokens(line) + spare > tokens` guard as later lines, with a fit fallback.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/guidance/charter.py:49

chunk_findings.detail: The new `held` rule lines are appended to `lines` before `_fit(rest, lines, budget)`, but nothing in this code ever checks whether those held lines themselves fit inside `budget`; `_fit` is only asked to choose more entries from `rest`. So whenever the reserved rule lines together exceed the supplied `Budget`, `inject` returns an `Injection` whose unpinned guidance is over budget. Example: with `reserve_rules=2` and a budget smaller than the two generated `_line(a, cap=BODY_CHARS)` strings, the two rules are still emitted and no `_fit` call can shorten or drop them. This contradicts the function contract `budget bounds the UNPINNED guidance` and the fix’s stated “inside the door budget”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/guidance/inject.py:196-198

chunk_findings.detail: When `charter` is non-empty and `len(charter) + 2 + len(note)` exceeds `budget * 4`, this function returns a payload larger than the documented `session.brief_max_tokens` budget. For example with `session.brief_max_tokens=50` (`budget * 4 = 200`), `charter="a"*160`, and any non-empty sections that force `trimmed=True`: `set_aside = 162`, so `cap = 38`. The note string is longer than 38 characters, so the backstop empties `text`, then the function appends the full `note` (`~83` chars) plus `"\n\n" + charter` (`162` chars), producing about `245` chars, which is `245 > 200`. The function’s own contract says the output is under `session.brief_max_tokens`; the charter is always preserved and never clamped, so this case overruns the budget.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/views/markdown.py:return text + ("\n\n" + charter if charter else "")

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert "r-pin" in got[0] and "pinned" in got[0]` is case-sensitive. The record is created with title `"Pinned law"`, and the expected charter line format in this same change is `[id] Title` (see `tests/test_guidance_inject.py`, which asserts `"[r-naming] Names"`). In `"[r-pin] Pinned law"` the lowercase substring `"pinned"` does not occur because the title starts with an uppercase `P`, so the test raises `AssertionError` even when the pinned rule is correctly retained and leads the list.

chunk_findings.detail: `lines()` returns the `MORE` fallback line without checking that `used + approx_tokens(more)` itself fits in `tokens`, and `block()` joins `HEADING`, `""`, and `LEAD` around `body` even though only `LEAD` and `body` were counted in `lines()`. The clamp at line 61 only limits the input token count, not the returned charter length. Concrete input: one live rule, `brief_max_tokens=2`, `rules_charter_tokens=1`. Then `tokens=1`, `used=approx_tokens(LEAD) > 1`, so `lines()` returns `["- _1 more rules: `ddflow rule list`_"]`; `block()` then returns `## Project rules\n\n` plus `LEAD` plus that line, which is far above both `rules_charter_tokens=1` and `brief_max_tokens//2=1`. This is the unresolved part of prior finding #1: the new guard stops the rule line from being emitted, but the fallback path can still make the charter exceed its documented budget.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/guidance/charter.py:50-63

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier refutation (“claim_rules_reserved is a floor taken from the budget first”) does not hold: the code appends the `held` rule lines to `lines` before `_fit` and never checks those lines against `budget`; `_fit` only chooses more items from the remaining `rest`. With `reserve_rules=2` and a budget smaller than the two generated `_line(a, cap=BODY_CHARS)` strings, `inject` still returns both held rule lines (and the cut line), so the unpinned guidance exceeds the budget that the docstring says bounds it. No clamp or subtraction was added, so the previous finding still stands.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/guidance/inject.py:197-198

chunk_findings.detail: The previous “clamp charter to brief_max_tokens//2” fix does not actually keep the returned pack under `session.brief_max_tokens`: with `budget=40`, non-empty sections, and `charter` at that clamp (~80 chars under the code’s 4 chars/token estimate), `set_aside` is 82, so `cap = budget*4 - set_aside = 78`, while the hard-coded `note` is 92 chars. The backstop slices to `max(0, cap - len(note))` = 0, empties `text`, appends the full `note`, and then appends `"\n\n" + charter`, producing 92 + 2 + 80 = 174 chars > `budget*4 = 160`. The charter clamp must be constrained by the remaining budget after `note` (e.g. `budget*4 - len(note) - 2`), or the charter must be inside the same backstop cap.

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion expects `CH.lines(rules, tokens=3, title_chars=100)` to return `["- _5 more rules: `ddflow rule list`_"]`. That sentinel line is 36 characters; using the repository’s 4 chars/token estimate, it costs about 9 tokens, so it exceeds the 3-token budget passed to `lines`. This means the probe for triage finding #1 does not actually answer the over-budget problem: a session with `session.rules_charter_tokens=3` (or any value smaller than the sentinel line) still gets a non-empty, over-budget charter body. The test should require either no body at all or a line that fits within the budget.

chunk_findings.detail: `AB.Facts.rules` is a string field: `ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py` still passes the `str` returned by `_governing` to it. The new launch-brief path sets `rules=[charter] if charter else []`, a one-element Python list. With any repo where `CH.block` returns non-empty text, `ddflow brief --for-agent` will render the prompt’s rules section with the Python repr of that list, e.g. `['[r-...]\n...']`, instead of the charter text. The new launch-brief regression check only asserts that charter ids appear as substrings, so it passes despite the corrupted rendering.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/briefing.py:86

chunk_findings.detail: The only cut line is `MORE = "- _{n} more rules: `ddflow rule list`_"`. It reports a count but none of the omitted rule IDs. B91e1d67c87's stated fix includes "a cut line that names ids"; this line leaves that part unfixed whenever the charter reserve is exhausted. Given 10 live advisory rules and a `rules_charter_tokens` value that fits only the first 3, `charter.block` emits `_7 more rules: ddflow rule list_` with no `r-...` IDs for the seven cut rules, so those rule records still do not reach the fresh session or the launch brief.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/guidance/charter.py:15

chunk_findings.detail: `block` caps the rule-line budget at `tokens = min(s.rules_charter_tokens, s.brief_max_tokens // HALF)`, but the rendered section also appends `HEADING`, a blank line, and `LEAD`; `lines` itself starts out with `used = approx_tokens(LEAD)`. If `rules_charter_tokens` is positive but smaller than `approx_tokens(LEAD)` (for example `brief_max_tokens=20`, `rules_charter_tokens=10`, one live rule), `lines` still returns a nonempty `[MORE]` body, so `block` emits a charter section whose token count exceeds both `rules_charter_tokens` and `brief_max_tokens // 2`. This violates the function’s own "never more than half" guard and the claim that the section is bounded by `rules_charter_tokens`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/guidance/charter.py:59

chunk_findings.detail: The new path appends `held` (unpinned, reserved rule) lines to `lines` before `_fit` is called. `_fit` only chooses from `rest`; it cannot remove or shorten lines already in `lines` without breaking the pre-existing pinned-guidance guarantee. So `budget` no longer bounds all unpinned guidance. For example, call `inject(..., reserve_rules=2, budget=Budget(chars=60))` with two rule records whose `_line(a, cap=BODY_CHARS)` lines are 40 chars each; `_fit` trims every non-rule record, but the returned injection still contains both full held lines (~80 chars), exceeding `budget`. The old pinned-guidance overrun is explicitly documented, but these reserved rule records have no such allowance.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/guidance/inject.py:200

chunk_findings.detail: The charter reservation is not bounded by the promised `session.brief_max_tokens` budget. When `len(charter) + 2 + len(note) > budget * 4`, the backstop computes a negative `cap`, truncates `text` to the empty prefix, appends `note`, and then returns `note + "\n\n" + charter`; that output is longer than `budget * 4`. For example, with `budget=10` (40 char budget), a fixed `note` of roughly 70 chars, and `charter = "r" * 200`, `set_aside = 202`, `cap` is negative, the final returned string is around 270 chars while the limit is 40. The function has no guard or precondition that `len(charter) + 2 <= budget * 4 - len(note)`, so a small `session.brief_max_tokens` or a charter larger than the reserved share silently violates the function’s own docstring.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/markdown.py:1129

chunk_findings.detail: The B91e1d67c87 regression requirement is that the claim block still lists the seven rule titles created by `_project`. This test only checks `len(got.records("rule")) >= cfg.session.claim_rules_reserved`; it never checks that `r-charter0`..`r-charter6` or their titles are present in the selected records or rendered claim block. A faulty fix that reserves the configured number of `rule` records but still leaves several `r-charter*` rules trimmed would pass this assertion, so the visible claim bug can persist without failing the regression test. It should assert each created rule id/title, not merely a count.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_guidance_budget.py:test_the_claim_block_reserves_slots_for_rules
